title: Microsoft Purview portal: service health dashboard
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says the Microsoft 365 page and Graph are the only documented service health controls, although its Azure reference documents alerts. It also asserts that the existing controls cannot govern the planned dashboard and that the dashboard is read-only without supporting documentation.

claims.quote: This new dashboard will combine the services and solutions health of Purview, Microsoft 365 services, and Azure Cloud Services in one central place in the Purview portal

claims.quote: As a Microsoft Purview user, you'll be able to view outages, service issues, and advisories that might impact your services.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; What's changing; Governance guidance; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 service health is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Health > Service health.
claims.quote: To view service health, in the left-hand navigation of the admin center, go to Health > Service health, or select the Service health card on the Home dashboard.

claims.claim: GET /v1.0/admin/serviceAnnouncement/healthOverviews reads existing tenant service health through Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/serviceAnnouncement/healthOverviews

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 service health page shows cloud service states and active incidents and advisories.
claims.quote: The Overview tab (the default view) shows all services, their current health state, and any active incidents or advisories.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rendered controls table
claims.claim: People assigned the Service Support admin role can view Microsoft 365 service health.
claims.quote: People who are assigned the Service Support admin and Helpdesk admin role can view service health.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rendered controls table
claims.claim: People assigned the Helpdesk admin role can view Microsoft 365 service health.
claims.quote: People who are assigned the Service Support admin and Helpdesk admin role can view service health.

claims.claim: Azure Service Health tracks Azure service issues.
claims.quote: Service issues: Problems in the Azure services that affect you right now.

claims.claim: Azure Service Health tracks planned maintenance.
claims.quote: Planned maintenance: Upcoming maintenance that can affect the availability of your services in the future.

claims.claim: Azure Service Health tracks health advisories.
claims.quote: Health advisories: Changes in Azure services that require your attention.

claims.claim: Azure Service Health distinguishes tenant-level and subscription-level event access.
claims.quote: Tenant access requires tenant admin roles and refers to the ability to view events that affect the entire organization. Subscription access, on the other hand, allows users with appropriate permissions to view events specific to the resources within a particular subscription.

claims.claim: The listed Graph operation reads subscribed services' health for a tenant and sets nothing.
claims.quote: This operation provides the health report of all subscribed services for a tenant. ... Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph lists ServiceHealth.Read.All as the permission for the operation.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | ServiceHealth.Read.All | Not available. ... Application | ServiceHealth.Read.All | Not available.

claims.claim: The planned Purview dashboard is read-only.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview portal service health dashboard read only incidents advisories services data. Opened Purview portal overview and read roadmap description. The roadmap promises viewing, but neither source states that the dashboard is read-only.
claims.fix: Remove 'Read-only;' from the summary. The roadmap documents viewing outages, service issues and advisories but does not exclude other actions.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; rendered controls table
claims.claim: The existing Microsoft 365 service health controls and Graph do not cover or govern the planned Purview dashboard.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview service health dashboard access setting PowerShell Graph API serviceAnnouncement. Opened Graph list healthOverviews and Purview portal overview. Neither states whether the new dashboard uses or is governed by existing service health access.
claims.fix: Replace 'Does not cover the planned Purview dashboard' in the row note and 'they do not govern the Purview dashboard' in the prose with 'Microsoft has not documented how these existing service health controls relate to the planned Purview dashboard.'

claims.claim: The only service health controls Learn documents are those of the existing Microsoft 365 service health page and Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Use the Service Health dashboard to create and manage Service Health alerts, which proactively notify you when service issues affect you.
claims.fix: Replace 'The only service health controls that Learn documents are those of the existing Microsoft 365 service health page and Microsoft Graph, shown in the table as today's alternative' with 'The table shows the existing Microsoft 365 service health page and Microsoft Graph as documented alternatives.' Retain the separate applicability qualification only as corrected above.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no change for end users.
claims.quote: As a Microsoft Purview user, you'll be able to view outages, service issues, and advisories that might impact your services.
